scope: LITD2 death, operation persistence and evolving corpse simulation

retry_chronology.principle: A run is a historical operation window containing successive real attempts. Death ends the current attempt, not the historical operation and not time itself.
retry_chronology.sequence: operation start -> real attempt -> death -> persistent corpse -> reconstruction delay -> return during the same unresolved operation window -> later real attempt -> objective resolution
allowed_changes: damage_or_blockage of local routes when causally justified
forbidden_changes: rewriting a failed attempt as if it never happened
restoring the battlefield to an earlier moment without cause
advancing to the next historical milestone solely because of death

corpse.loot_rule: Looted equipment is not deleted from the save. Important gear may move to an enemy, merchant, faction cache or recovery event. Unique narrative items can never be permanently lost through corpse evolution.
corpse.reanimation_rule: A reanimated corpse is the abandoned former body animated by an external or residual phenomenon; it is not the current protagonist and does not invalidate reconstruction.
corpse.self_echo_rule: Very rarely, a corpse can become an optional elite encounter using a partial reconstruction of the weapon and awakening profile from the attempt in which it died.
corpse.gore_integration: Cause of death, severed limbs, decapitation, burns and other body-state data feed directly into persistent corpse presentation and evolution.

safety_rules: No unique quest item can be permanently lost through corpse evolution.
A looted important item must remain recoverable through another route.
A reanimated corpse cannot permanently block mandatory progression.
The strongest self-echo encounters are optional or have an alternative path.
Corpse evolution never resolves a historical milestone by itself.
Corpse evolution never expires an important discovered side quest.
Corpse evolution can never make a save irrecoverable.
No retry may erase evidence that an earlier failed attempt physically happened.
history_rule: Historical progression occurs after successful completion of a milestone or explicit player progression, never because the player died.
narrative_rule: Permanent narrative consequences come from voluntary decisions and causally persistent actions; mechanical defeat does not rewrite history.
sarn_rule: The Night of Sarn is one historical operation window. A death ends that attempt; reconstruction takes real time and the next attempt returns to the still-unresolved Sarn operation under evolved local conditions. No time rewind occurs.
